title: The bug, reduced
blurb: Four operations, three replicas, no injected faults. Both writes go through n2 and end up with the same version stamp, so the two reads disagree about what happened.

title: The same bug, unreduced
blurb: The seed the fuzzer actually reported: five replicas, three clients, eighteen operations and every fault switched on. Reproducible, and unreadable — which is what the shrinker is for.

title: A network partition
blurb: The cluster splits, a minority keeps accepting requests it cannot complete, and the split heals. The fixed store stays linearizable throughout.

title: Nodes crashing and coming back
blurb: Replicas lose their volatile state and restart. Acknowledged writes survive, because that is what makes them durable state.

title: Everything at once
blurb: Loss, duplication, partitions, crashes, pauses and clock skew together. Still linearizable.

title: A healthy cluster
blurb: Jitter and reordering only. What the diagram looks like when nothing is wrong.
